summary: Liora reviews the nearly finished treatise and deliberately preserves contradictions and gaps rather than turning it into one complete doctrine.
panelPlan: Open in the hideout lab with versions, notes, and fragments covering Liora’s desk rather than one clean manuscript.
She compares several passages that point toward different legitimate practices after the collapse.
Liora starts to fill one gap, stops, and removes the attempted conclusion.
End on the unfinished space remaining visible inside the work.
directionInline: The incompleteness must look intentional, not like missing production material.

summary: Liora closes the final draft and states that future unity must be built through practice rather than borrowed from her authority.
panelPlan: Liora records one last note beside the deliberately open sections.
She places the fragmented final sheet among the rest instead of sealing a definitive version.
Close on Liora refusing to finish the gaps for future readers.
End on the treatise resting as a body of work that requires interpretation.
directionInline: This is Liora relinquishing control over how the text will be completed.

summary: Before the Resolve Circle meets, Iskari removes passages she believes would normalize unsafe improvisation.
panelPlan: Establish the Resolve Circle table covered by copies of Liora’s treatise.
Iskari reads a disputed section beside casualty and safety records.
She redacts or removes lines she believes cannot responsibly be endorsed.
End on her version already differing from the text Liora completed.
directionInline: Iskari’s edits should follow from the standards philosophy established in Issue 5.

summary: Ruvian adds engineering annotations that force the text to account for failure conditions and the realities of damaged infrastructure.
panelPlan: Ruvian arrives with field notebooks and lays them beside Iskari’s edited copy.
He marks diagrams and passages that assume equipment or resources no longer exist.
His practical annotations accumulate in the margins rather than replacing the whole text.
End on a second materially different version forming beside Iskari’s.
directionInline: Ruvian is correcting abstractions with lived breakage, not trying to author a rival scripture.

summary: Aveth insists the treatise include community-first logistics, leaving the Circle with three versions that each preserve a different meaning.
panelPlan: Aveth adds route and aid principles based on the trust networks now keeping convoys moving.
The three participants compare copies and realize none of them is merely a duplicate anymore.
No one agrees to collapse the changes back into one master text.
End on three annotated versions lying across the same table.
directionInline: The division should emerge through sincere attempts to make the text usable.

summary: At a fragile courier relay, Aveth prioritizes distribution of the treatise by need rather than status, immediately raising the question of who has authority to rank that need.
panelPlan: Wide relay post with limited copies and route lights flickering over multiple requesting worlds.
Aveth sorts destinations by survival need instead of prestige or former political position.
Couriers notice that some historically important worlds have been moved down the list.
End on Aveth stating that everyone gets the text, but not everyone first.
directionInline: Make scarcity, not ideology, the immediate cause of the dispute.

summary: A courier challenges Aveth to name the law that authorizes her priorities, exposing that even humane decisions now depend on contested legitimacy.
panelPlan: The courier points to the reordered list and asks who granted Aveth the right to decide.
Other couriers stop loading and watch because the answer affects every route.
Aveth has practical reasons but no surviving universal legal authority to cite.
End on the question hanging under unstable relay lights.
directionInline: Do not give Aveth an easy rhetorical victory; the legitimacy problem is real.

summary: A Shard node nearly fails after batteries from a Core cache arrive dead, turning resource exhaustion into an accusation of deliberate neglect.
panelPlan: Outer workers open Core crates expecting emergency batteries and find failed cells.
A node loses power while the replacement pack refuses to take load.
Ruvian’s crew braces a conduit as systems begin dropping.
End on Ruvian confronting the Core shipment as the immediate cause of the near-collapse.
directionInline: The evidence supports negligence or exhaustion, not proven sabotage.

summary: The outer technician demands power rather than explanations; Lochran denies sabotage and warns that interpreting every failure as intent will make cooperation impossible.
panelPlan: The technician points from the dead batteries to people working in the dark.
Lochran arrives or joins the dispute with records showing exhausted supply chains rather than a deliberate withholding order.
Ruvian remains unconvinced because repeated neglect has produced the same material result as hostility.
End on the three standing beside unopened Core crates and a barely stabilized node.
directionInline: Preserve the ambiguity: mistrust grows from accumulated experience even where intent is unproven.

summary: The Resolve Circle convenes around Liora’s treatise, and Liora rejects attempts to turn her writing into a mandate for any one emerging bloc.
panelPlan: Wide Circle meeting with the three annotated versions present and representatives grouped by increasingly distinct practices.
Liora sees passages being cited as authority for positions she never intended to crown.
She interrupts the attribution and states that the text describes work, not rule.
End on the room forced to debate without treating Liora as a final sovereign source.
directionInline: Keep Liora active: she challenges how her work is being used rather than passively watching.

summary: Iskari and Ruvian state incompatible necessities—standards that prevent repeated catastrophe versus improvisation that keeps damaged systems alive long enough to matter.
panelPlan: Iskari lays out the cost of errors made without shared standards.
Ruvian counters with environments where perfect compliance would mean waiting to die.
The Circle sees examples of both failures in the records around them.
End on neither position defeating the other because each answers a different lived danger.
directionInline: Stage this as collision between true constraints, not heroes versus villains.

summary: Aveth argues that neither standards nor repairs function without trust between people, and a Resolve engineer pushes the Circle toward a shared minimum rather than total agreement.
panelPlan: Aveth reframes the debate around who will carry resources, warnings, and responsibility between groups.
The Resolve engineer identifies the practical need for something every bloc can recognize without surrendering its own method.
Representatives stop editing doctrine long enough to consider one shared operational minimum.
End on the first move toward a symbol rather than a unified philosophy.
directionInline: The agreement should be narrow by design.

summary: The Circle places a unified safety sigil at the center of the table, but Iskari defines it specifically as responsibility rather than authority.
panelPlan: Representatives unveil or assemble a common sigil derived from the safety markings already in circulation.
The symbol sits between copies of the divergent treatise rather than replacing them.
Iskari accepts the mark only under a narrow meaning tied to responsibility.
End on others visibly reading more into the same image.
directionInline: The sigil is common form without common interpretation.

summary: Ruvian and Aveth accept the same sigil for different reasons—survival and the right to ask for help—locking ambiguity into the future symbol.
panelPlan: Ruvian touches or marks the sigil as something Shard crews can recognize without submitting to Core authority.
Aveth frames the mark as a promise of mutual aid across convoy routes.
The same symbol appears on three pieces of equipment or documentation associated with the different groups.
End on the identical mark carrying visibly different contexts.
directionInline: Do not visually unify the factions just because they share the symbol.

summary: Heska receives the three annotated treatise versions and recognizes that the archive can no longer honestly identify one uncontested original meaning.
panelPlan: Establish the pre-break archive vault with three containers prepared side by side.
Heska compares edits, redactions, and annotations across the versions.
No single copy can absorb all changes without erasing the history of disagreement.
End on Heska stating that history will inherit three truths.
directionInline: The archive problem echoes Issue 1, but now the contradiction comes from interpretation rather than timing.

summary: The archive curator chooses preservation over adjudication, sealing all versions so the future receives the argument rather than a fabricated certainty.
panelPlan: The curator refuses to designate one copy as authoritative without evidence that supports that claim.
Heska labels each version by provenance rather than correctness.
Separate containers close around the three texts.
End on all three entering the archive together.
directionInline: This should feel like an ethical archival choice, not indecision.

summary: As a prototype rescue vessel nears completion, Lochran argues that command should remain with Core because centralized authority historically held the network together.
panelPlan: Open in a damaged BHA facility with the prototype vessel visible or audible beyond the command area.
A field officer prepares a roster while Lochran places Core leadership at the top.
Lochran cites continuity of command as the practical answer to a multi-group crew.
End on the roster becoming another contest over what survives from the old order.
directionInline: Tie the command debate to an actual ship about to launch.

summary: The field officer rejects distant legitimacy and Iskari reframes the role as stewardship, leaving the ship ready before its command philosophy is settled.
panelPlan: The field officer points out that local crews follow people they know and trust, not inherited hierarchy.
Iskari challenges the premise that the new vessel needs old-style command at all.
The roster remains incomplete while engines begin their prelaunch cycle.
End on the empty captain field or unresolved command position beside a ship that cannot wait.
directionInline: Do not solve the future fleet structure here; establish the contested role that later fleets will answer differently.

summary: Engineers unveil the prototype multiworld rescue vessel as a working synthesis of components, crews, and route knowledge contributed by different survivor groups.
panelPlan: Large reveal of the prototype rescue vessel under stark emergency lighting.
Engineers show patched Shard-built systems integrated with route and safety equipment from other groups.
The Resolve engineer confirms the hull is ready despite unresolved politics.
End on crew movement beginning immediately because rescue needs already exist.
directionInline: The ship should feel practical and transitional, not yet the polished iconography of later fleets.

summary: Ruvian and Aveth assert that Shard crew and Verge routes are partners in the vessel’s mission rather than subordinate contributions, and the ship launches without a named captain.
panelPlan: Ruvian watches Shard crew board through one access point while insisting they are not passengers.
Aveth loads the Verge route-map into navigation and refuses to wait for a final central command settlement.
Ground crew clear the launch zone with the captain question still unresolved.
End on the prototype lifting away under shared but unsettled purpose.
directionInline: The launch works because the groups cooperate operationally without resolving ideology.

summary: From her hideout, Liora watches the rescue vessel depart with three different escort traditions already interpreting the shared sigil in different ways.
panelPlan: Establish Liora and Damiar at a distant observation point rather than at the official launch.
The prototype rises while three escort craft fall into formation behind it.
Each escort uses the shared sigil within a visibly different emerging visual and operational language.
Liora sees the divergence happening before the first fleet tradition is even settled.
directionInline: The escorts should foreshadow later fleets without pretending those mature factions already fully exist.

summary: Damiar recognizes that the launch is not a reunification but the beginning of many future fleets, each likely to claim a different meaning from the same inheritance.
panelPlan: Liora and Damiar watch the escorts separate slightly around the departing rescue vessel.
Damiar answers Liora by acknowledging that no future group will agree completely on what her truth meant.
The shared sigil remains visible on multiple craft even as their formations diverge.
Final wide panel: the vessels disappear toward different lanes of the broken network, turning one inheritance into multiple futures.
directionInline: End the six-issue prequel on divergence with continuity: many fleets, shared history, contested meaning.
